title: Privacy-aware mixture sampler for per-tenant calibration packs
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Problem: We need production-grade calibration datasets (per-domain / per-tenant) to validate INT8 and FP8 quantization profiles. Existing pack generation focuses on domain-only stratification and often leaks tenant-identifying tokens when we include live production prompts. This ticket designs and implements a privacy-aware mixture sampling pipeline that ensures representative coverage across intents/verticals while preserving tenant privacy and retaining tail/rare-intent signal for accuracy validation.
goals: 1) Produce per-tenant and per-domain calibration packs that are representative (intent coverage, token-length distribution, recency) and safe (PII redaction + entropy-preserving hashing). 2) Produce pack variants sized for different validators: small (10k prompts), medium (50k), and large (200k) with deterministic seeding for reproducibility. 3) Ensure packs exercise FP8 and INT8 profiles across typical sequence-length buckets and prompt/response length pairs.
constraints:
- Must comply with privacy rules: no clear-text tenant identifiers or direct PII allowed in training/calibration artifacts.
- Packs must be reproducible and auditable (seeded sampling + lineage metadata).
- Runtime budget: pack generation should complete for 50k size within 6 hours on our batch infra.
- Must integrate with existing storage (S3/secure-bucket) and access-control flows for Private customers.
proposed_approach:
1) Ingest production prompt stream (safe-mode) with redaction: apply a conservative NER-based redaction model, replace tokens with type-preserving placeholders (e.g., <EMAIL>, <PHONE>), then store a hashed tenant fingerprint (HMAC with key in KMS) rather than tenant ID.
2) Build a hierarchical mixture sampler: top level splits by vertical/domain; within each domain, mixture components are: (a) stratified reservoir sampling by intent cluster (semantic clusters via embeddings), (b) recency-biased reservoir (exponential decay alpha configurable), (c) rarity booster that upweights low-frequency intents (frequency floor), and (d) exemplar anchoring that ensures up to N canonical prompts per high-value class. Weights are configurable per tenant class.
3) Length and sequence bucketing: maintain token-length and (prompt,response) pair distribution constraints by bucketing (short/medium/long) and enforcing quota allocation per bucket.
4) Privacy-preserving tail retention: for low-volume tenants where full inclusion would leak identity, use differential sampling that mixes in domain-level pseudonymous exemplars instead of raw prompts.
5) Output pack metadata: seed, sampler weights, date range, effective sample counts per bucket, hash manifest, and link to lineage artifacts (confluence doc + PR).
6) Validation harness: run FP8 and INT8 quantized model inference on the pack, compute accuracy metrics (logit divergence, token-level top-1 drift, downstream task ECE, and generation-quality regression tests), and produce a calibration report with per-bucket failure modes.
acceptance_criteria:
- A pipeline produces deterministic packs for given seed and config (demonstrated with 3 seeds).
- Packs generated for a pilot tenant (internal test tenant) with sizes 10k/50k/200k and retained in secure S3 path with manifest.
- Validation harness runs on each pack and emits metrics: logit KL, top-1 token delta, and ECE; no bucket shows >8% degradation for INT8 on pilot model (or documented exception).
- PRs merged for sampler implementation and packaging scripts; Confluence doc with sampling parameters published.
- Security review completed and KMS key used for tenant hashing; audit log present.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Over-redaction removes useful calibration signal. Mitigation: Add a 'redaction diagnostics' pass that measures token entropy loss and flags buckets where more conservative redaction causes >5% token distribution shift.
Risk: Rare intents still underrepresented. Mitigation: Rarity booster component exposes tunable floor and we will run A/B runs comparing validation metrics with/without booster.
Risk: Generation time exceeds budget. Mitigation: run sampling in parallel shards and early-exit heuristics once quotas satisfied.
implementation_steps:
1) Prototype redaction + tenant-hash helper in Python (data infra spike) [Owen].
2) Implement mixture-sampler as streaming job (Rust) with per-shard quotas and deterministic reservoir (using seeded RNG).
3) Integrate bucketing and exemplar anchor ingestion (small Confluence schema for anchors).
4) Add output manifest and KMS-backed tenant fingerprinting.
5) Wire validation harness to runtime CI, add INT8/FP8 runner configurations and metric collectors.
6) Create runbooks and security review artifacts.
7) Pilot run for 2 internal tenants, collect metrics, iterate.

open_questions:
- Exact privacy threshold for tenant-level redaction: should we apply differential privacy noise for tenants with >X prompts? (input from Security).
- What is the canonical intent clustering model (use existing embeddings-service-v2 or run new fine-tuned clusterer)?
- Which downstream tasks should be included in ECE calculations (summarization vs. classification)?
